findings.comment:
4-101.11: Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

4-101.17: (A) Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE. (B) Hard maple or equivalent can be used for certain types of EQUIPMENT. (C) Whole, uncut raw produce and nuts shall be kept in wood shipping containers if received this way. (D) If nature of FOOD requires removal of protective outer layer, FOOD may be kept in untreated or approved treated wood containers. 

Observed a box of wood bowls out on a cart in the back hall. Bowls have a rough surface inside and seams that are not smooth where wood is woven. Replace these bowls with style that has a smooth easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 
Observed a can of soda to be sitting on the prep table next to the mixer and area where grape salad is being portioned. The can disappeared before something could be said about it. When questioned the employee sated that the can was placed there on the way back to the recycle. Do not place personal items, especially items that make it look like improper eating and drinking has taken place, on prep tables or other areas that should be considered clean for food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 
Observed several issues at the drink prep counter area between the ice machine and the drink cooler. The counter has developed some pits or been damaged since the last inspection, the wall behind the toaster has been gouged allowing for unsealed dry wall to be exposed. Repair these areas to be nonabsorbent.
Also, the fronts of the cabinets are starting to show wear and have areas that are not smooth. Repair cabinet fronts, counter and wall to be smooth, non absorbent and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Dish machine chemical dispenser is found to be providing 0ppm of chlorine to the dish washing unit. The technician is on site and working to correct the issue. Dishes done this morning will be rewashed so that they are properly sanitized. A new dish machine is being installed tomorrow. The new machine is a temperature sanitizing machine. If the machine can not be made functional, the staff will sanitize dished by hand in the 3 part sink. Machine tested at 100ppm Chlorine and the technician left. A valve had become plugged with crystalized chemical. Test dish machines daily to ensure that they are operating properly before use.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed foods in the small over/under cooler to be 50F. These foods are cut lettuce and various flavors of Smuckers jellies and toppings. The kitchen was instructed to call Smuckers to determine if the label marking, “refrigerate after opening” is for food quality or food safety.  It appears that the mark may be for quality. However, as this is a senior care facility they should check before determining weather to discard or keep these items. Some of the items are low sugar or sweetened with Splenda. Cut lettuce was discarded immediately. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 
This unit can be used for whole produce but nothing that requires refrigeration for safety shall be kept in this unit until it is repaired or 
replaced.

The 3 door unit along the front all is holding food between 40F and 43F. The time temperature control for safety foods were moved to the 3 door unit along the back wall and technician was called for repair. Repair or replace this unit and do not use it until it is able to maintain food at 41F or below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: Thermometers were absent from cold holding units. Provide thermometers to cold holding units to check air temperatures. 4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 An employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to manually dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed. Employee was later observed washing hands properly by preparing paper towels to dry hands prior to beginning the process and using the paper towels as a barrier after drying hands to shut off the faucet.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Forearms and elbows may also be used to shut off the faucet or dispense paper towels to avoid touching handles with freshly washed hands.

findings.citation_text:
4-602.12(B) Ceiling inside microwave was soiled with food splash. Ensure cleaning between uses or as needed daily to eliminate buildup.
 The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Lightbulbs at the back right corner of the dry storage area were dim to the point that a flash light was needed to see in that part of the room. Another set of lightbulbs were out in a kitchen fixture between the fridge and steam table. Manager noted lightbulbs get changed and then dim and/or burn out in a very short amount of time. Ballasts are old, and there has been discussion of redoing the lighting within the kitchen. In the meantime, ensure lightbulbs are changed as needed to provide adequate lighting in the kitchen and dry storage area. 
Light intensity shall be at least 10 foot candles (108 lux) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) PIC did not remove gloves for discard after adjusting face mask. Proper glove use was discussed with emphasis on glove changes after adjusting face masks. PIC washed hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solutions in sani-buckets were observed at a concentration of 100ppm and less than 50ppm. Bleach used to make solutions requires a concentration of 200ppm per the label directions. Bleach was added to both solutions to bring concentrations to 200ppm. 
-Dish machine final rinse concentration was inconsistent even after priming the chemical line several times and running multiple cycles. Concentrations were observed  at 10ppm, 50ppm, 0ppm, 50ppm, 10ppm, 100ppm, and back down to 10ppm and 0ppm. PIC made call for service, and technician arrived during the inspection. (see general comments for additional information)
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain sani-buckets at a concentration of 200ppm per the label directions, and maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions at no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14  (C) [Intake air / Exhaust air ducts (vents)] in the kitchen hood vent area were found with accumulation of dust on them. Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. The hood vent baffles are heavily soiled with dust. The sticker documents that they were last cleaned in December of 2018. This is likely outside of the manufacturer's specifications for cleaning and maintenance.  Clean hood vent regularly according to manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-101.11 (P) Plastic jugs used for tea are not recognized as a safe material for food-contact. Provide materials that are safe, durable, corrosion-resistant, non absorbent, resistant to pitting, chipping, distortion and are smooth to allow for easy cleaning. Reference 4-101.11.  Tea is being poured into plastic containers when it is hot and the containers are not of such material or durable for this use as they are warping and becoming distorted from this practice. Tea was placed into other pour able containers.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14. Employee was coached on hand washing practices.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The can opener blade is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). The can opener was washed, rinsed and sanitized in the dish machine.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at the dish area. The clean and sanitized food contact surfaces of utensils are being contacted by bare hands as they are being put into the dispenser. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11. The utensils were washed, rinsed and saniitized by the dish machine.
